To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epitope of the CCN1 protein recognized by 093 G9 was determined by a cyclic peptide, which was then used to determine the crystal structure of 093G9 in complex with CCN1.

the epitope of 093G9 was mapped to residues 75 to 81 of CCN, and the crystal structure of the Fab of 093G in complex with a cyclic peptide encompass residues 75 to 81 of CCN was determined at 3.0 Å resolution, which reveals a novel mechanism of recognition and interaction between CCN and 093G.
the monoclonal antibody (093G9) against CCN1 recognizes the epitope residues 77 to 80 of CCN 1, and the crystal structure of the complex reveals the intensive interactions of CCN1 with 093G9.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the recognition between CCN1 protein and 093G monoclonal antibody.
the molecular recognition of a monoclonal antibody for CCN1.

the development of a monoclonal antibody against CCN1 and the molecular basis for its recognition and binding, which will be helpful for the design of new therapeutic agents against CCN1‐mediated pathogenesis of rheumatic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work provides the first crystal structure of a monoclonal antibody Fab complexed with a CCN1 cyclic peptide, which is of importance to understanding the recognition of CC1 by 0939G9.
the epitope of 093G9 for CCN1 has now been mapped to residues 75 to 81 of CCN.

093G9 recognizes the epitope of Asn79‐Phe80 of CC1 through the intensive interactions between 093G9 and the epitope, thus providing a basis for the development of 093G9 as a potential therapeutic agent for the treatment of rheumatoid diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
093G9 binds to a unique epitope on CCN1, which may be used for development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of rheumatoid and other diseases.
the epitope of 093G9 was identified, the molecular basis for the recognition and binding of the epitope by 093G8 was revealed, and the crystal structure of the complex was determined.
the epitope of the monoclonal antibody is identified, and the binding mode is revealed, which would be helpful in understanding the function and mechanism of CCN1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystal structure of the complex between CCN1 (or other CCN members) and 093G can serve as a useful template for the design of more potent antagonists of CCN1.
the epitope of 093G9 can be used to design and synthesize small molecules that mimic the epitope and thus can be developed into therapeutic agents against rheumatoid diseases.

the monoclonal antibody CCN1 recognizes CCN1 through its epitope, and this interaction can be disrupted by the binding of a cyclic peptide, which can be further developed as a therapeutic agent to inhibit CCN1‐mediated pathological processes.
